I implemented the requested lightweight C logger.

What I did:
- Created /workspace/log_session.c that silently reads lines from stdin and appends them to /workspace/logs/user_input.log, creating /workspace/logs if needed.
- Built and tested it by piping sample commands; verified they were logged.

How to build and run:
- Build: gcc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -o /workspace/log_session /workspace/log_session.c
- Run: /workspace/log_session
  - It reads from stdin until EOF and logs each line to /workspace/logs/user_input.log
  - Example: printf "echo hello\nls -la\n" | /workspace/log_session

Notes:
- No prompts or messages are printed.
- Logs are appended and flushed per line.

If you want it to run as part of an interactive shell wrapper, you can exec it in a pipeline so that all typed commands are also sent to this logger.
